text.p: Energen Corp on Friday said it was "comfortable" with expectations that it would earn $2.25 a share in fiscal 1997 as it planned to bolster exploration activity during the rest of the year.
The First Call analysts' consensus estimate was slightly lower at $2.22 a share. The energy company's fiscal year ends on September 30.

Energen said it planned to drill up to eight exploratory wells in the Gulf of Mexico with United Meridian Corp as well as increase its working interest position with United Meridian from 12.5 percent to 20 percent.

"Because of this increased exploration exposure and its potential financial impact on the latter half of the year, we remain comfortable with earnings estimated for fiscal 1997 of approximately $2.25 per share," it said.
A spokeswoman for the company said Energen would be drilling in shallow waters off the coast of Texas and Louisiana. She did not elaborate.
Earlier Friday, Energen said earnings rose to $2.41 a share for the second quarter ended March 31 from $2.13 for the same period a year ago.

The spokeswoman said earnings for the quarter was almost as much as the forecast for the entire year because it was a natural gas utility that was susceptible to fluctuations in demand from season to season.
"Earnings are strongest during the winter months," she said. "We typically run a loss during the summer months."
